canDos.textEn: Can listen to a friend’s simple comments about their favorite sports and understand their reasons for liking it, what the attractions are, etc.
Can talk about the details of an event, while inviting a friend or responding to an invitation.
Can write a simple message to a friend or colleague canceling plans while giving the reason.
Can read and understand short and simple reviews about a manga.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about a film with comments or opinions.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about something you like, such as music or sports, including the reason and attractions.
Can look at the property information on a housing information website, and find the necessary information, such as rent, size, and location.
Can listen to simple comments from someone about recommended places to move to, and understand the reasons why they recommend them, etc.
Can ask a friend or colleague for help with moving, and can also accept or decline when someone else asks you to help.
Can report a problem that occurred in your building to the building manager, etc., and ask them to deal with it.
Can explain and complain to the property management company when a problem occurs in your apartment or condominium, such as noises.
Can respond to noise and other complaints from the property management company of your apartment or condominium, while explaining your situation.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about where you are living, such as how comfortable it is or the surrounding environment.
Can order food and drinks using the order tablet in a restaurant.

Can talk to a friend about a restaurant in Japan where you can eat the cuisine of your home country/region, including detailed information and reasons why you recommend it, such as what sort of restaurant it is and what you can eat.
Can write a simple post on social media about a restaurant you went to.
Can listen to an explanation about unfamiliar foods, such as local cuisine, and more or less understand what is said, such as cooking methods and origins.
Can listen to simple comments from a friend about recommended supermarkets, etc., and understand the reason why they recommend them, etc.
Can read an online article about eating habits and more or less understand what is written.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about your daily meals, such as what you eat and what you pay attention to in your diet.
Can listen to and understand simple advice, such as where to go or what to do, when you want to make new friends.
Can write a message to a friend who is in a club to get information about the club.
Can introduce yourself coherently, including your profile and hopes and aspirations for the future.
Can start a conversation with someone you are meeting for the first time, such as someone you will be working with.
Can talk in simple terms about yourself and the other person when a stranger tries to start a conversation.
Can read an online article about communication and more or less understand what is written.
Can talk in simple terms to a friend about your goals for Japanese learning and the reasons for them.
Can ask questions about an unfamiliar dialect you hear when talking with locals and others.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about your experience learning Japanese so far, including specific experiences.
Can read signs written in a local dialect and guess the meaning.
Can read multiple descriptions of online courses and apps on a Japanese language learning portal site and choose the ones that suit you.
Can exchange somewhat detailed information with a friend about Japanese learning methods.
Can write your profile, hopes, etc., in some detail on a site or app for finding language exchange partners.
Can listen to a friend’s simple explanation about what to do when picking up a lost item, etc., and understand how to respond.
Can look at a scam email and determine whether it should be ignored.
Can respond when asked to confirm your identity or to go through a baggage inspection at event venues, etc.
Can read and understand guides about Japanese lifestyle rules written for non-Japanese residents.
Can offer to help someone who appears troubled, such as being lost, using short and simple phrases such as だいじょうぶですか.
Can call 110 or 119 in an emergency and request the police or an ambulance using short and simple phrases.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about a difficult situation that happened to you recently, explaining what happened and how it was.
Can send birthday congratulations to a friend via a messaging app and exchange updates about how you have been recently.
Can listen to how friends and acquaintances have been recently and comment in short and simple phrases.
Can advise a friend in some detail about what to give for birthdays and other special occasions.
Can listen to speeches at wedding parties and other events and more or less understand what is said.
Can listen to and understand friends’ small troubles.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about the character and personality of close people, and how you met them.
Can consult with friends about troubles or listen to troubles and give specific advice.
Can read an article about interpersonal relationships and more or less understand what is written.
Can watch short travel-themed videos about famous places and local specialties and more or less understand what is said.
Can read articles introducing tourist destinations on travel websites and more or less understand what is written.
Can talk in some detail to a friend about desirable travel destinations, including places you want to visit and what you want to do there.
Can send messages to friends from travel destinations via a messaging app.
Can explain in some detail to hotel or inn staff circumstances and wishes and request services or changes.
Can talk in some detail about travel experiences to a friend.
Can give simple instructions and explanations about work to subordinates or junior colleagues at work.
Can read and understand bulleted documents about workplace rules.
Can convey in some detail to a superior your requests or complaints about your work or workplace environment during one-on-one meetings.
Can write messages to acquaintances to convey workplace problems in some detail and get information about where to seek consultation.
Can listen to simple comments about other people’s work and understand what kind of work they do and what they think about it.
Can listen to somewhat detailed communications and reports about work at workplace meetings or morning assemblies and more or less understand what is said.
Can look at job postings and find necessary information such as job content, salary, and workplace location.
Can talk in some detail about your abilities and what you can do in job interviews, etc.
